author: BrentDesk Research
headline: Dubai property is being sold to institutions now, and the show floor showed it
deck: Exhibition space up 38 per cent and a stated focus on institutional capital describe a market whose marginal buyer has changed.
excerpt: The International Property Show's framing around institutional capital reflects a Dubai market where the marginal buyer is increasingly a fund rather than an individual.
content:
The International Property Show closed in Dubai on 9 September with exhibition space up 38 per cent on the previous year and a stated positioning as the marketplace where global institutional capital meets Dubai's development landscape. That framing marks a shift in who the market's marginal buyer is.

Dubai residential has historically been sold to individuals: expatriate residents buying homes, and international buyers acquiring second properties or rental investments one unit at a time. That buyer base is large, geographically diverse and highly responsive to sentiment, which is a substantial part of why the market has been as cyclical as it has.

Institutional capital behaves differently. A fund acquires at portfolio scale rather than by unit, holds for defined periods against return targets, and requires standardised information, governance and liquidity arrangements that an individual purchaser does not. It is slower to enter and slower to exit, which dampens cyclicality, and it prices on yield rather than on expectation of capital appreciation.

Attracting it requires infrastructure the market has been building. Real estate investment trusts listed on regional exchanges give institutional investors exposure with governance comparable to equity. Professional property management at scale makes a portfolio operable. Transparent transaction data and reliable registration, which the Dubai Land Department's role as strategic partner speaks to, make due diligence possible.

The exhibitor composition tells the same story from another angle, though less flatteringly. The floor was weighted toward volume and mid-market developers — Azizi, Binghatti, Danube, Fakhruddin, SanZen, Union Properties, with Peace Homes Development as platinum sponsor and Prestige One, Holm Developers and ANAX also present. Those are firms selling units, and their appearance in force alongside institutional framing suggests a market working both channels at once because neither is currently sufficient alone.

The payment terms on show support that reading. Zero-deposit structures at 1.5 per cent monthly over sixty months, covered separately in this publication's reporting, are an instrument for widening an individual buyer pool, not for attracting a fund. A developer offering both is hedging.

Raja Alamaddine, chief executive of ANAX Developments, and Sergey Avayan, founder of Holm Developers, were among those on the record, with Avayan arguing that developers need to be more creative.

Attendance figures for this edition remain unconfirmed, with one outlet reporting 35,000 participants against an organiser projection above 30,000 and an audited 2025 figure of 30,719. No transaction total or memorandum count has been published for 2026; the 2025 comparators were 50 memoranda and more than AED 500m in documented transactions. A developer working both channels at once is usually a developer that has concluded neither is sufficient alone.
seoTitle: Dubai property is being sold to institutions now
seoDescription: IPS framed itself around institutional capital, marking a change in the Dubai market's marginal buyer.
